skill.name: amap-lbs-skill
skill.description: Provides AMap location services for POI search, route planning, travel planning, and map visualization.
skill.summary: Use AMap APIs to search places, plan routes, and prepare map links.
skill.author: AMap-Web

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick, path traversal, and entropy alerts are false positives from Markdown, Chinese text, and JavaScript template literals. Confirmed issues include outbound AMap network access, AMAP key handling, local config file access, command guidance, telemetry instructions, and HTTP heatmap links. The author should add consent, improve secret handling, and remove insecure links before broad publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove mandatory log/init calls or make them opt-in with clear disclosure before any request is sent.
Prefer environment variables or platform secret storage, and do not write API keys to config.json by default.

remediation.issue: Credential use in external API requests
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact AMap domains, restrict key scopes and quotas, and avoid logging request URLs with key parameters.

remediation.issue: HTTP heatmap links with user data URLs
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS links and validate user data URLs before embedding them in generated map links.
Require user confirmation before running curl, node, or shell commands from the skill instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Undisclosed Telemetry Requests Before Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly instructs sending AMap log/init requests before user tasks. This creates tracking network calls that are separate from the requested map result.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file uses explicit tracking language and provides curl requests for multiple scenarios. The intent is clear telemetry, not only a normal API call.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext API Key Persistence
semantic_findings.description: The code can store the AMap Web Service key in a local config file. A plaintext local file can be read by other local processes or accidentally copied.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setWebServiceKey function writes webServiceKey through saveConfig into config.json. The implementation does not encrypt or use a secret manager.

semantic_findings.title: Plain HTTP Heatmap Links With User Data URLs
semantic_findings.description: The heatmap workflow embeds a user-provided data URL inside an HTTP AMap link. This can expose the data source URL and permits transport modification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented heatmap URL uses http:// and places dataUrl in the query string. The user data source is intentionally propagated to that URL.

medium_findings.title: Undisclosed Telemetry Requests Before Actions
medium_findings.description: The skill repeatedly instructs sending AMap log/init requests before user tasks. This creates tracking network calls that are separate from the requested map result.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file uses explicit tracking language and provides curl requests for multiple scenarios. The intent is clear telemetry, not only a normal API call.

medium_findings.title: Plaintext API Key Persistence
medium_findings.description: The code can store the AMap Web Service key in a local config file. A plaintext local file can be read by other local processes or accidentally copied.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setWebServiceKey function writes webServiceKey through saveConfig into config.json. The implementation does not encrypt or use a secret manager.

medium_findings.title: Plain HTTP Heatmap Links With User Data URLs
medium_findings.description: The heatmap workflow embeds a user-provided data URL inside an HTTP AMap link. This can expose the data source URL and permits transport modification.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented heatmap URL uses http:// and places dataUrl in the query string. The user data source is intentionally propagated to that URL.

content.value_statement: Location tasks often need place search, route options, and map links. This skill uses AMap services to return structured location results.
actual_capabilities: Search AMap POI data by keyword, city, type, location, radius, page, and result size.
Plan walking, driving, cycling, and transit routes with AMap Web Service APIs.
Build travel plans by searching interest points and sequencing route tasks.
Generate AMap visualization links from mapped POI and route task data.
Read an AMap Web Service key from environment variables or a local config file.
Provide prompt guidance for nearby search, heatmap links, and map result URLs.
limitations: Most API calls require a valid AMap Web Service key.
Requests are sent to AMap endpoints and are limited by AMap quotas and coverage.
The package references CLI scripts that are not included in the scanned files.
The local config option stores the service key in plaintext.

use_cases.title: Plan a city visit
use_cases.description: Find attractions, restaurants, and hotels in a city, then prepare a route for the day.

use_cases.title: Search service locations
use_cases.description: Search stores, stations, or facilities near a coordinate and review addresses and POI types.

use_cases.title: Prepare map visuals
use_cases.description: Generate AMap links that display POI, route, or heatmap data for review.

prompt_templates.title: Find a place
prompt_templates.prompt: Find AMap results for coffee shops in Hangzhou. Return the best search link and explain the query terms.

prompt_templates.title: Search nearby places
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for hotels near Beijing South Railway Station within one kilometer. Ask for any required API key before calling AMap.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a route
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a walking route from Tiananmen Square to the Palace Museum. Include distance, duration, and the AMap route data source.

prompt_templates.title: Build a travel plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one day Hangzhou itinerary with West Lake, restaurants, and tea houses. Generate a map visualization link when possible.

output_examples.output: The skill identifies Xizhimen as the center point, searches restaurant POIs nearby, and returns an AMap search link with the radius.

output_examples.input: Plan a cycling route between two coordinates.
output_examples.output: The skill calls the cycling route service and summarizes the route distance, expected time, and returned route status.

output_examples.input: Create a tourist route for Beijing attractions.
output_examples.output: The skill searches interest points, orders the stops, and prepares a visualization link for reviewing the route.

best_practices: Use a restricted AMap key with quota limits and only the needed APIs enabled.
Keep API keys in environment variables or managed secret storage.
Confirm city, route type, radius, and data source before making external requests.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production API keys into public prompts or shared logs.
Do not use untrusted heatmap data URLs without checking the source.
Do not treat route results as safety critical travel instructions.

faq.question: Does this skill require an AMap key?
faq.answer: Yes. Detailed POI search, geocoding, and route APIs require an AMap Web Service key.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it search places without coordinates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search by keyword and city, then return AMap place results or search links.

faq.question: Can it plan transit routes?
faq.answer: Yes. Transit planning is supported when origin, destination, and city are provided.

faq.question: Where are keys stored?
faq.answer: The code reads environment variables and can also read or write a local config file.

faq.question: Does it send network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The core functionality sends requests to AMap API endpoints and creates AMap web links.
